title: Efficient Tensor Offloading for Large Deep-Learning Model Training based on Compute Express Link
problem: Large deep learning models exceed accelerator memory capacity, requiring tensor offloading to CPU memory. This creates two performance bottlenecks: coarse-grained tensor transfers that hide transfer overhead poorly, and redundant transfers that migrate unchanged data from CPU to accelerator unnecessarily.
motivation: Tensor offloading between CPU and accelerator memory is a major performance bottleneck when training large deep learning models that exceed accelerator memory capacity.
method: The paper proposes using Compute Express Link (CXL) to establish a cache coherence domain between CPU and accelerator memory. It extends CXL with an update cache-coherence protocol that eliminates unnecessary data transfers by tracking which data has changed, reducing redundant migrations and hiding transfer latency more effectively.
key_novelty: Using CXL-based cache coherence with an extended update protocol to eliminate redundant tensor transfers and reduce coarse-grained transfer granularity between CPU and accelerator memory.
contributions: Identifies coarse-grained transfer and redundant data migration as key bottlenecks in tensor offloading
Proposes CXL-based cache coherence domain architecture between CPU and accelerator
Extends CXL with update cache-coherence protocol to track and avoid unnecessary transfers
Achieves 33.7% training time reduction (up to 55.4%) over DeepSpeed without affecting convergence or accuracy

metrics.accuracy: No degradation; maintains model convergence and accuracy

primary_theme: CXL-based cache coherence for efficient tensor offloading
